questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Italy, Italian food and wanted to be able to explore a country within Europe further. I also wanted somewhere not too far away, so that I will have a "second home" where I can easily come back.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a little bit tricky to find information about when classes would actually start. Our classes for science started on october 1st, which was two weeks later than people who took social sciences. But this just wasn't stated very clearly anywhere.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The coordination office in Milan was helpful when we wrote emails about courses and information, but the answer was often that the information wasn’t available yet (the Italian way).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found an appartment together with some friends, and we just talked to students who had been to Milan on exchange before us. I also recommend looking at this early in the process. We used a company called Italianway that I can definitely recommend.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Milan is a big city but the metro works pretty good (just not after 00:30 or when there is a strike) so if you live close to the metro you should be able to get to school pretty easily.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process was very difficult since the course schedules weren’t available until very late. It was difficult to find classes where the schedules would work out with not too many overlaps. Sometimes they were in different locations as well.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was a bit difficult since there was almost no information in advance. I spent to much time choosing classes I wanted before going and then found up the schedules wouldn't work.  At least it is very easy to go to some different classes the first couple of weeks and not choose anything definitely. They are very loose in that sense, you can go and experience the teacher, see the location and learn about the course before you have to decide on anything. Registering the courses on the Milan course registration could be done about one month into the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, we found everything on the website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful since the schedule couldn’t work out. I wanted courses from some different master programs and the classes were just overlapping too much or had ECTS points that didn’t add up.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don’t be too set on the classes you want and therefore also don’t stress about choosing classes on your application or anything beforehand. But maybe have a list of interesting classes that you want to check out when you arrive. And then you can find out what the schedule is like, exam type and the location once the information is available. Also maybe choose more classes form the same master program will be helpful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think for biomedical science, University of Milan just isn’t that good. I do not regret going to Milan!! And I also learned some interesting stuff but I think overall don’t choose Milan if you are going for the academic program.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were easy to follow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is boring. There were mostly lectures, and then one course had a three-day lab assignment but that was the only change from the classroom lectures. Classes were very small, about 10-40 people (maybe because the master programs were small). Most teachers were sitting down while teaching. Also there is no scheduled break in a two hour lecture, some teachers stop 15 minutes early but you never really know, and sometimes they just talk for 2 hours straight. 

Exams are also very different. It was difficult to get any information about the form of the exam and we had no previous exams/example questions to use for studying. For oral exams, they are typically done in front of the rest of the class, which sounds worse than it actually is, but be prepared that it is different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cell therapy and gene silencing (7 ECTS)
Genetics, cellular and molecular biology (12 ECTS) 
Molecular bioinformatics (6 ECTS) 
Molecular pharmacology and immunology (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Cell therapy and gene silencing because the topics covered were interesting and the teachers were better. It is also part of a master program that I would encourage to do more classes with, since it had more of a “class-feeling” compared to the other programs. This class also has a lab part which I thought was a nice activity (and not very difficult). Bring your own lab coat if you choose a lab course!

 I do NOT recommend "Genetics, cellular and molecular biology" if there is still a teacher named Luisa. She hated Erasmus students and was the worst teacher I have ever experienced. 

I also don’t recommend Molecular bioinformatics if you want to actually learn programming or anything practical, as it is very theoretical and didn’t give me the bioinformatics skills that I was hoping for (also for preparing for the Master). 

Molecular pharmacology and immunology was alright, some interesting topics and the professors were okay.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Gym membership was way more expensive than expected. Looked at many different places and it was like 100 euros per month + 100 in signup fee. Transportation is cheap, 165 DKK per month for unlimited travel in Milan.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn’t seek any of this but I think there were some. But not as much as in Denmark. E.g. no “fredagsbar” with the uni.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus organization had a lot of social activities for exchange students to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Maybe try and join Erasmus activities. I think it is a good place to meet different people, especially from lots of different places.

Me and my friends bought the membership card at the beginning for €16 but never attended a single event, so just consider whether that is something you're interested in.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go see the Dolomites. I was sad that I didn't go in the fall when it was still warm enough to go, because once winter comes, the hiking routes close down. Everyone said it was really beautiful! And take the train/flixbus around the country, it is very easy and cheap. I arrived in September when it was still very warm and I would recommend going to the coast around Genoa to go to the beach. 

Also try to book a time slot to see The Last Supper painting that is in Milan. It is very cheap (2€ for students) but the slots fill up early, so try to book it long time in advance. Going to football games at San Siro stadium is also pretty cheap for most of the games, so you can go see Inter or AC Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was easy, except for accepting that the pace is just slower in Italy and there is less structure. Class schedules and course registration is done last minute and the classes might start on time or 15 minutes late, you never know. 

Most young italians speak English, and with time you will learn a few words that help you get by.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do it! I tried to do it a little too late. Just ask to go have an aperitivo after school, it’s very informal and everyone is welcome.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I thought the teaching methods for the most part were boring and unstructured, and I think the lack of structure is what was most challenging to me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and they like going out and meetup. They go out for business lunch, go out for aperitivo after school/work and go out for dinner and drinks. It is also a lot cheaper than in Denmark, so enjoy!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don’t go for academics, go for the food, living in a big city and the beautiful country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don’t stress about course registration, you will figure it out once you get there. Classes might be in different locations so remember to look at that. 
One thing I would also recommend is to not spend too many weekends having visits from back home. I had my family and friends wanting to visit me, but remember to say no to some, so that you can spend your weekends going on trips and exploring the country more. I spent too many weekends as a tour guide.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I thought it was really cute to make so many new friends and meet so many new people. There are many Danish students in Milan, and everyone is really open so you have many opportunities to hang out and talk to new people. Just remember that everyone is here for the same thing and do some friend-dating!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having enough money for travelling:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
